title: Assistant Bash fails on Windows selector event loop: host commands must not use asyncio subprocess APIs
answers: Assistant Bash tool says subprocesses are unsupported on Windows
NotImplementedError when Assistant runs a shell command under multiworker or reload server on Windows
Codex or Claude bash tool call fails on Windows with selector loop
asyncio create_subprocess_exec not supported Windows MLflow assistant
body:
Symptom: On Windows, when MLflow runs with the selector event loop (multiworker or reload server), Assistant Bash tool calls fail instead of running the command.
Root cause: mlflow/assistant/providers/tool_executor.py:_execute_bash_on_host used asyncio.create_subprocess_shell / create_subprocess_exec, which the Windows selector loop does not implement.
Fix pattern: Keep the same argv/shell decision but run the command with subprocess.run inside asyncio.to_thread, passing shell=full_access, stdout/stderr=PIPE, cwd, env and timeout=120. Replace asyncio.TimeoutError handling with subprocess.TimeoutExpired.
Constraints: Applies to host-side execution in _execute_bash_on_host only; sandboxed execution is a different path. Any new host subprocess call in this module should follow the same thread-plus-subprocess.run pattern rather than asyncio subprocess APIs.
applies: Host-side Assistant Bash execution in mlflow/assistant on any event loop, especially Windows.
says: Assistant fails to execute shell commands when running on Windows servers
Terminal actions in the assistant crash when the server runs in reload mode on Windows
Assistant reports that running command line tasks is unsupported on Windows multiworker instances
Allow the AI assistant to run host commands reliably on Windows systems
search: Host-side Assistant Bash command execution in mlflow/assistant/providers/tool_executor.py:_execute_bash_on_host must use subprocess.run inside asyncio.to_thread instead of asyncio subprocess APIs on Windows selector loops. Commands run with shell=full_access, stdout and stderr set to PIPE, cwd, env, and a 120-second timeout catching subprocess.TimeoutExpired. Applies exclusively to host-side execution in _execute_bash_on_host, leaving sandboxed execution paths unaffected. Any new host subprocess execution in this module must follow the thread-plus-subprocess.run pattern to prevent NotImplementedError on Windows multiworker or reload servers.
